extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, EPA reviewers, and owners/operators of fossil fuel-fired steam generating units (utility boilers and IGCC units)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER), the degree of emission limitation achievable, subcategorization, applicability, and presumptive standards of performance for existing fossil fuel-fired steam generating units under CAA section 111(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the BSER
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA must 'determine[ ],' taking into account various factors, the 'best system of emission reduction which . . . has been adequately demonstrated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine the BSER, the EPA identifies systems of emission reduction (e.g., control technologies) that have been adequately demonstrated and evaluates the potential emissions reduction, costs, any non-air health and environmental impacts, and energy requirements. The Agency may create subcategories where sources differ by characteristics relevant to suitability of controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emission limitation achievable
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA must 'ascertain the degree of emission limitation achievable through the application' of the BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emission guidelines must identify the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the BSER (typically numeric), because states then establish standards of performance 'that reflect' that amount. The preamble emphasizes that the EPA historically provided numeric degrees in prior emission guidelines and that a boundless or range-only approach is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: States' standards of performance must reflect EPA-determined degree
rubrics_metrics.description: States must establish 'standards of performance' for sources that are based on the degree of emission limitation the EPA determines in the emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once EPA determines the BSER and the degree of emission limitation, 'the States then submit plans containing the emissions restrictions that they intend to adopt and enforce in order not to exceed the permissible level of pollution established by EPA.' States' standards must be at least as stringent as corresponding emission guidelines (see 40 CFR 60.24(c), 60.24a(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review criterion for state plans — 'satisfactory' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA approves state plans if the standards of performance are 'satisfactory' under CAA section 111(d)(2)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA's basis for finding a plan 'satisfactory' includes that the plan contain 'emission standards . . . no less stringent than the corresponding emission guideline(s).' The Agency warns against an approach that limits review to procedural criteria, noting EPA must review substantive adequacy so states cannot set 'extremely lenient standards' by meeting only procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF (remaining useful life) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: In applying a standard to any particular source, a State may consider 'among other factors, the remaining useful life of the existing source to which such standard applies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory provision allows states to account for remaining useful life when setting standards of performance for particular sources; it is referenced as part of the required EPA/state process (discussed further in section X.C.2 of the preamble).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization based on relevant source characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may create subcategories under CAA section 111(d) where sources in a category differ by characteristics relevant for suitability of emission controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA considered fuel type, planned cessation dates, and capacity factor as relevant characteristics and finalized subcategories for coal-fired, oil-fired, and natural gas-fired steam generating units (and further subcategories by intended operation horizon and capacity factor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal-fired steam generating units — BSER: CCS with 90% capture
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating units, the EPA determines CCS with 90 percent capture of CO2 meets BSER requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of this BSER results in a degree of emission limitation equivalent to an 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). The compliance date for these sources is January 1, 2032. EPA evaluated cost reasonableness assuming long-term operation and appropriate amortization periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal-fired steam generating units — BSER: 40% natural gas co-firing
rubrics_metrics.description: For coal-fired units that plan to permanently cease operations after December 31, 2031 and before January 1, 2039 (medium-term), the EPA determines natural gas co-firing at 40 percent of annual heat input meets BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of this BSER results in a degree of emission limitation equivalent to a 16 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). EPA determined co-firing at 40% entails less capital infrastructure than CCS, can be implemented by January 1, 2030, and has costs comparable to or less than EPA's cost-reasonableness metrics for sources with limited amortization periods (more than 2 years and up to 9 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for coal-fired units ceasing before January 1, 2032
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired steam generating units demonstrating that they plan to permanently cease operation before January 1, 2032 are exempt from the 40% co-firing requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded that the amortization period for such units (2 years or less) is generally too short for co-firing costs to be comparable to EPA's cost-reasonableness metrics, so these units fall into an applicability exemption (i.e., they are not subject to the rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-reasonableness assessment and amortization-period consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA evaluates costs of controls (e.g., CCS, co-firing) using fleet-average annualized costs and considers the amortization period available to sources based on their intended operation horizon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CCS, annualized fleet average costs are comparable to prior metrics when amortization period is more than 7 years (operating past Jan 1, 2039). For sources with shorter available amortization periods (e.g., ceasing before 2039), annualized costs are higher; these differences inform subcategorization and BSER selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas- and oil-fired subcategories based on capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalized subcategories for natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units based on annual capacity factor (base load, intermediate load, low load).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because units with similar annual capacity factors perform similarly, EPA sets different BSERs and degrees of emission limitation for base, intermediate, and low load subcategories and provides presumptive standards accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for base and intermediate load natural gas- and oil-fired units — routine O&M
rubrics_metrics.description: For base load and intermediate load natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units, EPA finalizes BSER of routine methods of operation and maintenance and a degree of emission limitation of 'no increase in emission rate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provides presumptive standards of performance: base load sources (annual capacity factor ≥45%) presumptive standard 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross; intermediate load sources (>8% and ≤45%) presumptive standard 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross. Compliance date: January 1, 2030 for all natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for low-load oil- and natural gas-fired units — lower-emitting fuels
rubrics_metrics.description: For low load oil-fired sources (annual capacity factor <8%) and low load natural gas-fired sources, EPA finalizes BSER of lower-emitting fuels with degrees of emission limitation defined on a heat-input basis: 170 lb CO2/MMBtu (oil) and 130 lb CO2/MMBtu (natural gas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumptive standards equal these heat-input-based limits (170 and 130 lb CO2/MMBtu).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standards of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provides presumptively approvable standards of performance based on the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the BSER for each subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While states establish standards, EPA's table (Table 1) lists presumptive standards (e.g., 88.4% reduction for long-term coal, 16% for medium-term coal, 1,400/1,600 lb CO2/MWh for gas/oil base/intermediate, 130/170 lb CO2/MMBtu for low-load) and refers to section X for detailed discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated facility applicability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'designated facility' is any fossil fuel-fired electric utility steam generating unit that: (1) was in operation or had commenced construction on or before January 8, 2014; (2) serves a generator capable of selling greater than 25 MW to a utility power distribution system; and (3) has a base load rating greater than 260 GJ/h (250 MMBtu/h) heat input of fossil fuel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'designated facility' is used to refer to sources affected by these emission guidelines. The rationale parallels that for 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'existing source' and treatment of modifications/reconstructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 111(a)(6) defines an 'existing source' as any stationary source other than a new source; emission guidelines do not apply to units new after Jan 8, 2014 or reconstructed after June 18, 2014 (the subpart TTTT applicability dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is finalizing that a modified coal-fired steam generating unit would be considered 'new' (and thus not subject to these emission guidelines) if the modification occurs after the date the proposal was published in the Federal Register (May 23, 2023). Units modified prior to that date remain existing sources subject to the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from requirement to establish standards under a state plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EGUs that may be excluded from the requirement to establish standards under a state plan include nine categories (e.g., units subject to subpart TTTT from qualifying modifications, units with federally enforceable permits limiting net-electric sales, non-fossil fuel units with certain permits, CHP units with limited sales, small-serving units, municipal waste combustors subject to subpart Eb, certain solid waste incineration units subject to subpart CCCC, EGUs deriving >50% heat input from certain industrial processes, and coal units electing to permanently cease operation before Jan 1, 2032).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed exemptions mirror many current exemptions in 40 CFR 60.5509(b) and are discussed further in section VIII.E.1 of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan content and required plant-specific data (ACE Rule procedural model discussed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the ACE Rule approach (criticized here), states were required to 'evaluat[e] each' candidate technology and provide a summary 'which include[s] an evaluation of the . . . degree of emission limitation achievable' and a variety of plant-specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required data fields included the plant's annual generation, CO2 emissions, fuel use, fuel price, carbon content, operation and maintenance costs, heat rates, electric generating capacity, and timeline for implementation. EPA explained the purpose of these data was to 'adequately and appropriately review the plan to determine whether it is satisfactory.' The preamble criticizes the ACE Rule for relying on procedural requirements without providing a BSER or specific degree of emission limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity requirement — numeric degree, not broad ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission guidelines should identify with sufficient specificity the BSER and the degree of emission limitation achievable; providing ranges (or '0 to >2%') that allow arbitrary state choice is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains the ACE Rule's presentation of HRI as seven 'candidate technologies' with wide ranges of percentage improvements (including effectively unbounded ranges) shifted responsibility to states and left EPA without a benchmark to evaluate plans. EPA emphasizes prior guidelines included numeric limits and that the agency must explain departures from that practice.
